title: Winnie-the-Pooh
author: A.A. Milne
short_summary: In the Hundred Acre Wood, a gentle, honey-loving bear named Winnie-the-Pooh spends his days with his friends: worried little Piglet, gloomy Eeyore, wise (but often wrong) Owl, and busy, organizing Rabbit. Their adventures are small and simple — but always end up more complicated than anyone expected.
extended_summary:
In the Hundred Acre Wood, a gentle, honey-loving bear named Winnie-the-Pooh spends his days with his friends: worried little Piglet, gloomy Eeyore, wise (but often wrong) Owl, and busy, organizing Rabbit. Their adventures are small and simple — but always end up more complicated than anyone expected.

Pooh gets stuck trying to leave Rabbit's house after eating too much honey, the friends set off on an "expedition" to find the North Pole without really knowing what it is, and everyone pitches in to find Eeyore's missing tail. Through it all, Christopher Robin, the boy who owns all these toys come to life, is always nearby to help sort things out.

questions.prompt: What does Pooh get stuck in after eating too much honey?
questions.explanation: Pooh eats so much at Rabbit's house that he gets stuck halfway out of the front door on his way home.

questions.prompt: Pooh's best friend, a small and often worried animal, is simply called ___.
questions.explanation: Piglet is Pooh's closest friend, even though he is often nervous about their adventures.

questions.prompt: Match each character to their personality.

right: Gloomy and always expects the worst
Acts wise but often gets things wrong
Organizes everyone and likes being in charge

questions.explanation: Each friend in the Hundred Acre Wood has a distinct personality that shapes how they handle their small adventures.

questions.prompt: Sort each character into the right group.

content.groupA: An animal living in the Hundred Acre Wood

questions.explanation: Christopher Robin is the human boy whose toys come to life as his animal friends in the Wood.

questions.prompt: Why do you think Christopher Robin's friends keep going on adventures together even when things often go wrong?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the friends seem to enjoy being together and helping each other more than getting things exactly right.

questions.prompt: When Pooh has 'a rumbly in his tumbly,' what does that usually mean?

options: He's hungry and thinking about honey
He's about to go on an expedition
He's had too much honey already

questions.explanation: A 'rumbly in his tumbly' is Pooh's own way of saying he's hungry — which, for Pooh, usually means honey isn't far from his thoughts.

questions.prompt: The friends set off on an 'expedition' to find the North Pole without really knowing what a North Pole actually ___.
questions.explanation: Not knowing exactly what they're looking for has never stopped the Hundred Acre Wood friends from a good adventure.

questions.prompt: Put Pooh's honey mishap in order.

items: Pooh visits Rabbit's house and helps himself to a very large amount of honey
He tries to leave through Rabbit's narrow front door
He gets completely stuck, halfway in and halfway out
His friends have to help pull him free

questions.explanation: It's a classic Pooh problem: too much honey now means too much trouble later.

questions.prompt: Match each friend to the small adventure they're best known for.

right: Gets stuck in a doorway after eating too much honey
Loses his tail and everyone helps look for it
Organizes the group, whether they asked for it or not

questions.explanation: Each small adventure in the Hundred Acre Wood fits the friend at the center of it perfectly.

questions.prompt: Sort each line into the right group.

content.groupA: Sounds exactly like something Pooh would say
content.groupB: Doesn't sound like Pooh at all

options.label: 'It's always a good time for a little something to eat'
'I never worry about anything, especially not honey'
'I'd rather skip breakfast and get right to work'

questions.explanation: Pooh is famously food-focused and slow to worry — the two 'not Pooh' lines are exactly backward from how he really is.

questions.prompt: Pooh's adventures are always small and simple, but they still end up feeling like real adventures to him and his friends. What's a small, simple moment in your own life that felt like a little adventure?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the Hundred Acre Wood suggests that adventure doesn't have to be big to feel real.
